# Photosynthesis

## Light reactions

Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. In plants it takes place in chloroplasts, which contain the pigment chlorophyll. Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green light. The light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes and produce ATP and NADPH.

## Calvin cycle

The Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to build sugar from carbon dioxide. It takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast. The Calvin cycle does not use light directly, but it depends on the products of the light reactions. Oxygen is released as a by-product of splitting water during the light reactions.
